questions.question: Explain why is a SAR ADC commonly used in mechatronics?
questions.solution_html:
• Explain at least 2 points. (2.5 marks) each
  • The Successive Approximation Register (SAR) ADC is one of the most widely used
  • analog-to-digital converters in mechatronic applications because it provides an
  • excellent balance between speed, accuracy, and power consumption. The SAR ADC
  • converts an analog signal into a digital form by comparing the input voltage with
  • successively generated reference voltages using a binary search algorithm. This method
  • enables moderate-to-high conversion speed with high resolution, typically between 8
  • to 16 bits.
  • In mechatronic systems, real-time data acquisition is critical—for example, when
  • sensors continuously monitor position, temperature, or pressure. The SAR ADC’s fast
  • conversion time allows the microcontroller to quickly process signals and generate
  • control actions. Moreover, its relatively low power consumption and compact size
  • make it ideal for embedded mechatronic devices, such as robotic systems, motor
  • controllers, and instrumentation modules.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Describe the importance of controllers in a mechatronic system.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the role of controllers in detail – (5 marks)
  • Controllers are the “brains” of a mechatronic system. They process data received from
  • sensors, compare it with the desired set point, and generate suitable control signals to
  • drive actuators. This ensures that the system performs its intended function accurately
  • efficiently, and safely. Common controllers used in mechatronic systems include
  • microcontrollers, PLCs (Programmable Logic Controllers), and PID (Proportional
  • Integral-Derivative) control units.
  • For example, in an automatic robotic arm, the controller continuously receives
  • feedback from position sensors and adjusts motor movements to achieve precise motion
  • control. Controllers also handle decision-making, timing, and safety monitoring.
  • Without controllers, the interaction between mechanical and electronic components in
  • a mechatronic system would be uncoordinated and unreliable, leading to poor
  • performance or system instability.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Identify the medium used in pneumatic systems and explain?
questions.solution_html:
• Medium identification – (1 mark). Explanation – (4 marks)
  • The working medium in pneumatic systems is compressed air. Air is readily available
  • non-polluting, and safe to use, which makes it an ideal choice for industrial automation
  • and mechatronic systems. Pneumatics relies on the energy stored in compressed air to
  • produce linear or rotary motion in actuators such as cylinders and motors.
  • Compressed air is easy to transport through pipelines and can be stored in reservoirs
  • for continuous operation. Pneumatic systems are commonly used in manufacturing
  • lines, robotics, and packaging machines where quick, repetitive motion is required.
  • Additionally, the system components are relatively simple and robust, which makes
  • pneumatic systems reliable and cost-effective for automation applications.
questions.final_answer: pneumatic systems reliable and cost-effective for automation applications
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Show how would you use a potentiometer to measure angular position?
questions.solution_html:
• Show how would you use a potentiometer to measure angular position.
  • Explanation the working of a potentiometer and how it measures the angular
  • position – (5 marks)
  • A potentiometer can be used as an angular position sensor because its resistance
  • varies linearly with the rotation of its shaft. When a constant voltage is applied across
  • the potentiometer terminals, the output voltage taken from the wiper terminal changes
  • proportionally to the angular displacement of the shaft. This forms a simple voltage
  • divider circuit that provides an analog voltage corresponding to the angle of rotation.
  • By interfacing the output voltage to an analog-to-digital converter or microcontroller
  • the system can accurately determine the angular position. This method is simple, low
  • cost, and widely used in applications such as joystick controls, robotic arms, and servo
  • motor feedback.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is the role of an anti-aliasing filter?
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the working of anti-aliasing filter – (5 marks)
  • An anti-aliasing filter is a low-pass filter placed before an analog-to-digital converter
  • (ADC) in signal processing systems. Its main function is to remove or attenuate high
  • frequency components of an analog signal that are above half the sampling frequency
  • (known as the Nyquist frequency). If these frequencies are not filtered out, they can
  • “fold back” into the lower frequency range after sampling, creating distortion called
  • aliasing.
  • In mechatronic systems, signals from sensors often contain unwanted high-frequency
  • noise caused by environmental factors or electrical interference. The anti-aliasing filter
  • ensures that only the relevant frequency components of the signal are converted into
  • digital form, preserving signal integrity.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain Mechatronics with suitable application.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain mechatronics and its components – (5 marks), Any one application -(5 marks)
  • Mechatronics is an interdisciplinary field combining mechanical engineering

  • automated machines. Instead of treating these areas separately, mechatronics integrates
  • them to achieve higher precision, reliability, and flexibility in modern systems such as
  • robots, automobiles, and smart devices.

questions.question: What are the typical applications of FIR filters in signal processing?
questions.solution_html:
• Define IIR filter – (2 marks). Applications – (8 marks)
  • A Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filter is a type of digital filter whose response to an
  • impulse settles to zero in finite time. It is widely used in signal processing due to its
  • stability, linear phase characteristics, and ease of implementation in both hardware
  • and software. Unlike IIR (Infinite Impulse Response) filters, FIR filters do not have
  • feedback loops, ensuring inherent system stability.
questions.final_answer: feedback loops, ensuring inherent system stability
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: List and explain different types of proximity sensors used in automation.
questions.solution_html:
• List and explain different types of proximity sensors used in
  • automation.
  • Explain at least 4 types. (2.5 marks) each
  • A proximity sensor is a device used to detect the presence or absence of an object
  • without making physical contact. It operates by emitting and receiving energy fields such
